subject: environmental-science
title: Scope 1, 2 and 3
welcome_lead: Direct, electricity and supply-chain — slice the carbon accounting cake.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions accounting.
final_note: Scope 3 is often the largest — and the most overlooked carbon liability.

concepts.def: Direct emissions from owned/controlled sources (fuel, fugitive).
Indirect emissions from purchased electricity, steam, heat or cooling.
All other indirect emissions in the value chain (15 categories per GHG Protocol).
Carbon dioxide equivalent; common unit converting all GHGs via GWP.
WRI/WBCSD standard for corporate carbon accounting since 2001.
Emissions per unit output (e.g., kg CO₂e per kWh).

walkthroughs.body_html: Scope 1 covers on-site combustion. Scope 2 reflects energy purchased. Scope 3 captures suppliers and product use.
For retail, Scope 3 often dominates (>80%). For utilities, Scope 1. Identification guides effective reduction.
GHG Protocol provides scopes framework. ISO 14064 standardises quantification and verification.

mcqs.q: Why is burning fossil fuels considered to disrupt the carbon cycle?
